utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence wanted to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and I think we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdjevic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his examination. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to spend some time talking about the situation in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps during the time-period of 1993 to 1994. First of all, what knowledge do you have of the establishment of the so-called safe areas in the Drina Corps's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, three safe areas were established: Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to the establishment of these safe areas, what kind of enemy forces had been operating in these same areas?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the eastern part of the front line of the Drina Corps there was the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina with its command in Srebrenica. In the broader area of Gorazde there was also a formation of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its rank was that of a division.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to the enactment of the safe areas, what had been going on between those forces and your own?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before these territories were declared safe areas, there was combat between the Army of Republika Srpska and these mentioned forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the broader area of Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What instructions did the Drina Corps receive from its commander upon the enactment of these aforementioned safe areas?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What instructions did the Drina Corps receive from its commander upon enactment of the safe areas, how was the corps supposed to behave or implement anything on its side?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the Drina Corps, after the establishment of these safe areas, were given strict orders to stop at the lines attained because certain negotiations were to follow, the demilitarisation of these safe areas, or rather, the disarming and demilitarisation of these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, what was your observation of how the enemy side implemented these negotiations on demilitarisation of the safe areas?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally, as officer for the organisation of communications, took part in these operations and I was personally at the forward command post when an order arrived from the commander of the Drina Corps, stating that all further activities should be halted and that these areas would be demilitarised. However, after that date, all the time, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde showed that demilitarisation had not been carried out at all and their military activities had actually continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What was the Drina Corps's assessment of the number of enemy troops based within the safe areas - and I'm now just focusing on the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intelligence that the Drina Corps had at the time indicated that in that area the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had armed forces that were equivalent to a division consisting of five brigades with roughly 15 -- 12- to 15.000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a clarification, Mr. Lukic -- Mr. Ivetic. 12- to 15.000 in the brigade or in the whole division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entire division that consisted of five brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you said a few moments ago, sir, that the military activities of those armed forces within the safe areas continued. How frequent were those military activities launched from within the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the forces of the 28th Division, according to evident information received through intelligence and reconnaissance, they remained in their positions with weapons directly aimed at the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska; however, what was most characteristic was the communication that existed between their enclaves, that is to say, two safe areas with smaller or larger armed groups. They communicated between Srebrenica along the route towards Tuzla and this other one towards Kladanj, that is to say, the central part of their armed forces through the territory that was controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska. Also, they communicated between two enclaves, Srebrenica and Zepa. This communication for the most part was concealed because of their own interests, because of their intentions. However, many times during these communications they carried out ambushes and sabotage activities that resulted in the killing of our soldiers and civilians in the areas through which they communicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you talked about information received through intelligence and reconnaissance. Do you yourself have any personal knowledge and experience in relation to these types of activities of the armed forces from within the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally had several such experiences because the Drina Corps very often because of that kind of situation organised searches of the terrain along the routes where these sabotage groups communicated, and I was invariably the communications officer in charge of these activities. And several times I took part in these activities. As a matter of fact, during the war, sometime in 1995, the Drina Corps decided to deal with Stublic, a particular feature between Srebrenica and Zepa, namely, to place a point of resistance there at company level; and I personally went there to secure the communications for these soldiers. Their exclusive task was to prevent the movement of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina between Srebrenica and Zepa. On that day when I was on that mission, it was just by chance that I managed to avoid an ambush because the vehicle behind mine was ambushed and soldiers of the Milici Brigade were killed and wounded in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What did the Drina Corps do in relation to these attacks and incursions? Did anyone contact the United Nations or UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that this situation was being resolved in a diplomatic way or at least that was the attempt that was made because there were members of the UN in the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa and they were supposed to ensure demilitarisation and - how do I put this? - to prevent any kind of combat activity coming from the enclave. From that point of view, the activities of the Drina Corps and the political structures of Republika Srpska were aimed at trying to stop this combat activity coming from the enclaves through a diplomatic effort through UNPROFOR, that they rein them in, that they stop the activity of these sabotage groups from the enclaves and their entry into our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to look at 65 ter 1D2980 in e-court with you. Sir, this is dated the 5th of April, 1994, from the command of the Drina Corps and is an order for raising combat-readiness to the highest level. And according to the first paragraph in both versions, it says: "According to highly probable information at our disposal, it is possible that enemy forces will carry out a general attack from the north-west. We are unable to specify exactly the axis of the main strike aimed at linking up with the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, and it is also possible and probable that enemy forces from the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa will attack our forces in order to relieve their forces at the front." First of all, do you recall the situation that is reflected in this order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For us, officers of the Drina Corps, this was a generally known situation concerning the intention of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to link-up their main forces in that part of the front line, specifically their 2nd Corps in Tuzla, with the enclaves, Srebrenica and Zepa. This offensive, or rather, this operation would be carried out through simultaneous attacks by their main forces in Tuzla, the 2nd Tuzla Corps, that is, and an attack by the 28th Division from Srebrenica and Zepa. That is something that the Drina Corps that was in that area did know and its main task was to try to prevent that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did an attack of this nature actually occur at some point in time subsequent to April 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These attacks were permanent; however, to the best of my knowledge, none of them resulted in such strength that would result in the linking up of the enclaves with the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. However, the Drina Corps was constantly encumbered by these activities and this combat in the rear of its territory, if I can put it that way, which made it less possible for them to do their fighting at their main front, the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've described for us the truth -- troop strengths of the forces from within the enclaves. What about these enemy forces situated in the north-west, did the Drina Corps have an assessment as to the troop strength of those forces?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know certainly that in the western area the forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina were far more numerous. There is -- their command of the 28th Division was in Tuzla, because the capacity of that area, speaking in demographic terms, is very high; but as for specific information about the troop strength of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina there, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to look at item number 4 in this order and here it talks about some type of encryption -- standard TKT encryption. Could you explain for us what encryption protection is being discussed herein?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the usual orders, if I can put it that way, mentioned in warfare as such; namely, that all activities -- not only in war but also in peace time but particularly in war time, in order to protect the data from anyone who may find them to be of interest, that protection of all communications should be done -- should be carried out by protecting this information. In this specific case it has to do with general documents of encryption. This TKT abbreviation means secret command of troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I seek clarification. A minute ago you told us that the command of the 28th Division was in Srebrenica and just a few -- a short while ago you told us that their command was in Tuzla. Now, do you have an explanation as to why you first referred to Srebrenica and now refer to Tuzla as the location of the command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 28th Division with its command in Srebrenica was directly subordinated to the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla; that is to say, the superior command of that division is the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say the command over the 28th Division was in Tuzla, whereas the command of the 28th Division was in Srebrenica. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this time we would tender this document, 1D2980, as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D903, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up 1D2979 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, this is dated 6 September 1994 and is again issued on behalf of the Drina Corps to several units. First of all, in relation to the commands that this order is directed, to what formation do they all belong?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these commands to which this order is addressed are brigades of the Drina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in the first paragraph of this order it talks of intelligence that new groups of Muslims from Srebrenica and Zepa were leaving in the direction of Kladanj and Tuzla. First of all, we've mentioned Tuzla in relation to the forces to the west. Where is -- where or what was located in Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kladanj, the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were located there as well. This was territory under the control of the Muslim-Croat Federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, just one clarification. The document says "they were preparing to leave," this is different from what you said, "they were leaving."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise if I misspoke. Yes, it does say "preparing to leave" in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, what kind of groups are we talking about here, what was the nature of these groups that were believed to be preparing to leave these two enclaves?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were sabotage groups from the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. They took paths that were well-known to them through uninhabited areas and through the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps they moved towards Tuzla and Kladanj. In the beginning of my testimony today I said that according to our estimates and according to what was going on in the field, the main problem that we encountered from these groups were their ambush and sabotage activities along the road that linked that eastern part of Republika Srpska to the western part. They carried out ambushes very often, attacks, with a view to disorganising the territory, keep our troops busy, and force us to mop-up the terrain, which was a pain-staking activity. And we had to keep our forces on the ready in that part of the area and front.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: These sabotage groups that you say the corps encountered, how large would they be in terms of the number of personnel that were within them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to some information that I personally had in that period and according to intelligence available, those groups varied in size. Frequently these would be groups of fighters from Srebrenica and Zepa whose families had moved to Tuzla in 1993, so they would desert from their units intending to reunite with their families. Also frequently those were sabotage groups with the exclusive purpose of carrying out ambush and sabotage actions to destabilise our main route, the main route used by the Drina Corps that was also crucial to the whole of Republika Srpska because that road was taken by civilians, by vehicles, buses, trucks, all kinds of traffic. So according to the information I had at that time, these sabotage groups had a whole range of different intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were such sabotage groups posing a threat to the Drina Corps; and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They posed a permanent and enormous danger to the Drina Corps, not so much in terms of their troop strength but the outcome of their activities because not a single unit could feel safe and plan actions in their main area and on their axis of activities and defence with such a sabotage group hanging over them. Every commander knows that such sabotage group could be sometimes as large as a brigade, and he cannot divert his main strength to deal with that group and put all his other activities on a back burner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document, 1D2979, as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D904, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Before you move on I would have -- if you have done with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the document you have explained is all about sabotage groups, but the order doesn't refer to sabotage groups at all, it just says groups of -- new groups of Muslims. It doesn't say anything about sabotage groups or whatever they were consisted -- did you also have information about other groups leaving, including civilians, for example, who would leave -- who wished to leave in the direction of Kladanj and Tuzla or was such information not received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After 1993 when -- with the escort of UNPROFOR, according to our information, a group of civilians, after the arrival of General Morillon, moved out of their own accord using UN vehicles. It was their own initiative, but I never had information that at any point in time civilians had gathered and wanted to use the road between two enclaves. So this order, as far as I'm concerned, refers exclusively to sabotage groups. It's written in military language, it's a military order signed by General Zivanovic, and it could only refer to sabotage groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether there's any documentary evidence which would support your interpretation, that is, intelligence reports which specifically point at sabotage groups? I'm first asking the witness, Mr. McCloskey. If you -- unless there's anything wrong with my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, it's a perfectly good question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not seeking compliments, as a matter of fact, but there's no objection to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to -- the witness to respond to it. Could you answer my question whether you have such -- whether you are aware of the existence of such documentary evidence supporting your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about documents, but I have personal experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answers my question. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If it would help the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution does believe there were such groups - you'll recall Mr. Butler's testimony on this point - and that they were designed to do much of what this witness is saying they were designed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this brings me to another question which is on my mind already for some time and that is: To what extent is this a matter in dispute? We hear now evidence, but -- it's my recollection that, for example, military -- that we heard quite a lot of evidence about 28th Division members going out of Srebrenica and doing all kind of -- I remember torching villages, et cetera. And I -- my recollection tells me that there was not often a fierce cross-examination on that, that it would not have happened. Therefore, it came to my mind to what extent are we listening to evidence in relation to matters which are not in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Even more so, much of this was part of the Prosecution's case through Mr. Butler. Now, we have not said anything thus far because I think forming this as a foundation to get into more areas of dispute is fine as long as we're not taking too much time. At that point is when -- when you had the specific question I thought it would be good to clear up that that is not an item in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, I was about to ask such a question, but then these specific answers triggered me to put the question as I did. Mr. Ivetic, apparently we are listening to a lot which is not really in dispute. Is there any reason to spend time on matters which are not in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we've been introducing documents to show the progression of matters, and indeed in the documents we've had specific questions as to the encryption that was discussed in the other documents. So I believe to show the picture of the progression of events the -- although not in dispute, the specific facts of the same need to be understood. For instance, here we're talking about groups, that's why I wanted to know what types of groups. There are other documents, I believe, that talk about groups, and although not in dispute, it has not been said on the record precisely that these documents talking about groups are talking about military groups. And that's why I wanted to clarify that with the witness, who has knowledge of these things from his time within the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Matters which are not in dispute, Mr. Ivetic, should take no or hardly any time. And to know more details about matters which are generally not in dispute is not of great assistance to the Chamber. Again, I leave apart some exceptions here and then. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, sabotage groups as has been discussed by the Prosecution and the Defence is not in dispute. That this document refers to sabotage groups would be in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There we have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. So you do challenge that this document is talking about sabotage groups or is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe I may be talking about the previous one where you pointed out that it wasn't talking -- that there was no mention of sabotage groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that is this one. This is talking about new groups of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what my question was focused on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct. We do challenge that this has to do with sabotage groups, but we don't challenge sabotage groups generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but not in this document. Okay, that has been clarified. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'd like to not be able to hear Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I clearly stated. Mr. Ivetic, could you -- apparently --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Stojanovic is not ... no, no discussions. Then we go back to the little pieces of paper. Mr. Ivetic, if Mr. Mladic just ignores two, three times that we had a rather liberal regime on consultations, then next time we might be in a position that we have to go back to the little notes written down for communication. I think it's not necessary, but it depends on Mr. Mladic's own behaviour. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do we have 1D2990 in e-court. Actually, I will skip that document, since I think we've raised that with the prior document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you about the road Jasenovac-Zeleni Jadar. After the safe area of Srebrenica was formed, within whose control was that road, or rather, the territory where that road was located?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the control of the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska, namely, the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did that remain true for the entire duration of the existence of the safe areas or did it change at any time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Srebrenica was declared a safe area and after the UNPROFOR arrived, a clear boundary of these protected areas was established, whereas the warring parties remained on two different sides of the areas. This part, Jasenovo, remained outside of the protected area in the territory of the Drina Corps, that is to say, the VRS. Initially, because of their unfavourable tactical position, the units of the Drina Corps deployed in that area did not deploy their forces ahead of that road so that the road would be behind them. So there came a moment when the forces of the 28th Division from Srebrenica began to take advantage of that and to enter that interim area which housed some installations and businesses such as Zeleni Jadar company, and they started carrying out sabotage actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to look at 1D2981 with you. While we wait for it, it's dated the 3rd of January, 1995, and is issued by the Drina Corps command. And it talks in the first paragraph before the order begins of the enemy from Srebrenica using the signed agreement on cessation of fire to seize important features and it refers to the area of Bracan to Zeleni Jadar. How did this area relate to the territory and road that we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These features mentioned in this document are geographical, topographical features, they are far out of the protected area of Srebrenica along the route to Zepa. I remember this time very well because I was designated in that place to organise communications. Our units did not have enough forces to keep their positions on these features permanently, to have permanent points of resistance there, and these are very dominating features, very good from a military point of view. Therefore, the command of the Drina Corps estimated that the 28th Division did not respect the truce that was signed and the demilitarisation agreement, and they could advance towards these features and occupy them using their dominant position. During the implementation of this order, I personally was assigned to organise communications and I was there, present, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D905, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to look at 1D2983 with you. This, you'll see, is dated a few months later, 18 March 1995. And here we have the formulation in the first paragraph, talking of equipment being taken from a sawmill in Zeleni Jadar or it being dismantled by -- dismantling equipment from the sawmill in Zeleni Jadar and taking it away and has the formulation "Turks." Who is this reference in relation to? Who was it that was dismantling and taking away this equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Srebrenica that were referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in this initial paragraph it says that UNPROFOR has not done anything to -- has so far not done anything to prevent such behaviour, and then in items 1 and 2 of the order it says that the task of preventing such actions should be undertaken "with the help of UNPROFOR, and if that does not yield results, UNPROFOR is to be warned that this will be prevented by force." Do you know if the Drina Corps did, in fact, undertake efforts to work with UNPROFOR to prevent these types of things?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel Vukota Vukovic did that very often. He had frequent meetings with UNPROFOR and he was located precisely in the area of Srebrenica and this territory around Zeleni Jadar belonged to his area of responsibility. I also believe that all the other political means were used for that purpose. The reckoning was that an agreement had been signed, that it was a protected area, and that UNPROFOR would do that job and prevent sorties of these armed units from Srebrenica. These assaults and the looting of property controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I at this point in time put a question to the witness, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, in the first paragraph in the penultimate line we see the term "Turks." What does this term refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That expression was used very often in the war and it can be found in a number of very official military documents as used by the commanders. "Turks" is a reference to members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In similar documents on their own sides they called members of the VRS "Chetniks," and some of the commanders on our side called members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina "Turks." And if I may add a personal explanation, I suppose that neither side minded too much. There's nothing offensive in this expression. Even today when the national team of Turkey is playing in Sarajevo, everybody's cheering the Turks, everybody in Sarajevo shares that feeling. Even once in Mostar there was a big quarrel when there was -- there was a fist-fight when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you went far beyond by question, but one term you used is not recorded. You said even today when the national team -- did you say of Turkey is playing in Sarajevo? Was that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anywhere where the Turkish national team is playing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. That is clarified. In one of the previous documents we saw a reference to Muslims. Why was it used here not in this document, the term "Muslims"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Each commander who wrote a document used his own discretion in the choice of terms, but in the bulk of documents the opposing side is referred to as "the enemy," not "Turks," not "Muslims," but "the enemy."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- one clarifying question as well. Witness, you explained that you expected UNPROFOR to do something about this dismantling of facilities. Just for my proper understanding, do I understand that the factory or the facility was outside the demilitarised zone but was not under real control of the VRS? Is that -- now -- I see you are nodding yes. What is it now exactly that you are blaming UNPROFOR for, for not -- for allowing them to leave the demilitarised zone and do this -- undertake these activities of dismantling activities outside the demilitarised zone or do you blame them for not having intervened when that happened outside the demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not blaming anyone. I only know that it was their duty because UNPROFOR was in the buffer zone and they had their check-point on that road from Srebrenica to Zeleni Jadar. Behind their backs was the boundary of the protected area and the forces of the BH army. It was logical to expect them to prevent armed members of the BH army from Srebrenica from passing by them, entering the area of the VRS, and taking equipment from there because such activity could lead to conflict. And the job of the UNPROFOR there, as I understand it, was to supervise demilitarisation and prevent conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you expected them to stop those who would undertake actions to enter through the buffer zone. Did you also expect them to intervene if something happened outside the buffer zone and, as you said, the area of the VRS? I mean, were they within their mandate allowed to follow those who left and then intervene in the VRS zone or is it that you say, no, they should have stopped them even from entering that zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, they should have stopped them from entering the buffer zone, and obviously that check-point of the UNPROFOR was on the asphalt road. They made incursions across that road, entered our area, looted and robbed, and went back, but the first attempt to stop it should have been made by UNPROFOR peacefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm looking at the clock. Could you tell us where we are in terms of time? We happily have a witness who gives direct, focused, and concise answers. That's an advantage, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe that I will finish within the time-period that we had set forth for this witness, perhaps even a little earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- and where are you as far as you yourself are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe we had approximately 25 minutes yesterday and we've had approximately, I believe, 45 to 50 minutes today, so that should get me approximately halfway, a little over halfway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because your time estimate was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three hours. Yes, we are close to one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar confirms that you are still within the one -- you are not yet at 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's nevertheless appreciated that you assume that we are at 50 per cent and nevertheless perhaps finish earlier. Witness, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up P2100 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, I can tell you, sir, that it is dated the 3rd of June, 1995, originating from the forward command post in Pribicevac of the Drina Corps command. And if we can first quickly look to the second page, we will see, sir, that this document purports to have your signature. Now, if we could move back to the first page and if we look at the item under 1, "Enemy," it reports a forceful expulsion of UNPROFOR from the Zeleni Jadar post. And then in the second paragraph under 1, it talks about: "Inhabitants of Zeleni Jadar moving out in panic following UNPROFOR's withdrawal, with large groups of people (probably civilians) observed in the afternoon moving from the general area of Zeleni Jadar and Pusmulici towards Srebrenica." First of all, sir, do you have any observations about the accuracy of the reporting of these events in this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we look at the next page, do you have any comment as to the signatory of this document being listed as yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this operation that was being carried out by the Drina Corps, I personally was at the Pribicevac forward command post. It was not actually an operation. It was a combat activity that was commanded by the corps commander, General Zivanovic. When I testified previously, I had the opportunity to see the order for this operation and it pertains to taking full combat control over the Zeleni Jadar-Jasenovo road. In that combat order it was stated that General Zivanovic, Colonel Stojan Veletic, chief of artillery of the Drina Corps, and I as someone who was in charge of organising communications were to be in command. When I testified before years ago, I had the opportunity to familiarise myself with this document as -- and as an officer I was taken aback, if you will, by this report on an operation that was commanded by General Zivanovic, corps commander; and there are two colonels who are also at the command post with him. I, as a young major then, was supposed to write a report on that combat activity. On the other hand, I was taken aback by the considerable amount of misinformation in that report because I know what the actual situation was at the time. There was a lot of exaggeration, and as far as officer speak is concerned, I was taken aback by the illiteracy of officers writing up this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the short answer, sir, if we understand you well, is that you are not the signatory to this document? Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you identify for us any items that you consider to be inaccurate or exaggerations in this report, and perhaps we can go back to the -- well, you could tell us -- you could tell us what parts you consider to be inaccuracies or exaggerations in the reporting of these events.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well - how do I put this? - this combat activity was carried out during the course of a single day, that is to say, it lasted only one day. Usually in the war-time period I would remember things that seemed unusual to me, and I remembered that event, namely, that this combat activity was carried out without a single bullet being fired. Quite simply, our forces within their territory moved from one position to another and this road which was important to us thereby was left behind us and then our supplies could take place along that route. Further on in this report it is absolutely incorrect that in this area, this small place called Zeleni Jadar, and there was in the buffer zone before this combat activity was carried out, it was not true that civilians lived there, the civilian population. Because first of all, this is a place with a few very small factories and a few houses. And I never heard or saw in any area of Bosnia-Herzegovina that the civilian population would live in a buffer zone, that is to say, between the weapons aimed at the two warring parties against one another. So I claim with full responsibility that the civilian population did not live in the buffer zone and, panic-stricken, they could not have moved towards Srebrenica. Also in this report there is a reference to some activities about firing, then even the movement of tanks and APCs of the enemy in Srebrenica. And we know full well that the 28th Division in Srebrenica did not have any usable tanks and APCs, and so on and so forth. So it is my general assessment that most of this report was written with a lot of exaggeration and whoever it was that wrote this probably wanted to exaggerate his own contribution to these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic. Witness, the first question in relation to this document that was put to you was whether -- whether you had any observations as to the accuracy of this report. You said "no." And then after that you start claiming the inaccuracy. I have difficulties in reconciling your first answer which says: No, I have no observations on it, and then start saying that it's all wrong what is written down there. Do you have any explanation why you first answered that you had no observations about the accuracy of the reporting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my understanding was that the lawyer, Mr. Ivetic, asked how accurate this report was and to what extent it was accurate, whether it reflects the actual situation on the ground, as compared to what is written here. So that is why I said that the actual situation on the ground is not reflected in the content of this report. So that's why my answer was no. So in my view, this report is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you also said that the inhabitants of Zeleni Jadar could not have left in panic because you thought that -- there were no inhabitants, and you explained that by saying that you'd never seen that anywhere else, that in such a zone people were living and that therefore they couldn't have been living there. Now, that's a conclusion, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is just something that supports my assertion that they did not live there. So I just supported my assertion by saying that it didn't happen anywhere else either, but at first I did say that they did not live there, namely, that in Zeleni Jadar there was no civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I was at the forward command post while this combat activity was taking place. It lasted only for a few hours within the course of a single day, and quite simply I was listening to all the reports coming in from the units that were carrying out this combat activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it was not reported that people were living there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly, and that they were not living there and also that there was no one leaving that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this is all invented by those who wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any explanation as why they would invent these kind of things which would -- could lead to all kind of problems. If your report is not in accordance with the reality what's -- you take enormous risks. Any explanation for why they would have invented this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That remained as a question in my mind as well, in view of the fact that at the command post General Zivanovic was there, Colonel Veletic, and Colonel Vukota, and I as the fourth officer there. So I believe that this report could have been written only by General Zivanovic or one of these two colonels, and I would like to hear their view why this report was written this way because it does not reflect the actual situation at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are so pertinent in that, where you say you -- you didn't sign the report, it was just sent on your behalf without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Somebody who wrote up this report at the end of the report just typed out my name. The order from a day or two before this date for carrying out this operation, that order has the personal signature of General Zivanovic. In my view, this was written by someone who wanted to show that he had achieved some kind of major military success there, if I can put it that way, by commanding this kind of action. And there were many exaggerations here, many things that are absolutely inaccurate and they are verifiable because you can take the reports of the 28th Division from Srebrenica for that day about our movements or about the withdrawal of civilians. Also you can take UNPROFOR reports, they were in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To some extent I think what you're telling us is speculation, but you draw our attention to the possibility to verify that. And I take it that the parties take that seriously, that we can see whether other reports support your thoughts that it may be exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we please see the bottom of the original, please, the end of the original. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One small question. In the beginning it says after the "expulsion of UNPROFOR." It doesn't say exactly who expelled UNPROFOR. Could you tell us who did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that when this combat activity started, in that buffer zone there was an UNPROFOR check-point, that is to say, on the road between Zeleni Jadar and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand all that, but I would like to know who then pushed them out from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, from a military point of view, if they were pushed out this only could have been done by the members of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do you know or do you not know? Is this again a conclusion or is it knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is my knowledge, quite simply, that these forces of ours that were carrying out this activity literally wanted to make it known to UNPROFOR that they don't want any kind of clash with them, but that in their own area, that is, within the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, they wish to place our forces on the line so that this road would be placed under our control; that is to say, the intention of the Drina Corps was not any kind of conflict with UNPROFOR, only -- only for them, I mean, to allow us to put our positions up on the territory that belongs to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me read it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you go back to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So under the heading "Enemy" where it reads: "After a successful operation and the forceful expulsion of UNPROFOR from the Zeleni Jadar post, the enemy was observed systematically building up large forces ..." That refers to UNPROFOR being forcefully expelled from the Zeleni Jadar post by your forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what is referred to in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have one short follow-up. Your assessment about this document was - that can be found on page 26 - that somebody who has written this report wanted to exaggerate his own contribution to these events. Why is it that this person, this unknown person, used your name if he wanted to show how good he was in combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the letter-head of this document, you see that the report was sent to the command of the Drina Corps, to the Chief of Staff personally; that is to say, somebody wanted -- I mean, reports are never sent to the corps command to the Chief of Staff. Somebody wanted to fascinate or to show before this Chief of Staff their --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I stop you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- achievements as an officer or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: My question was a little bit different from your answer. Why didn't this person, this unknown person, didn't use his own name by signing if he wanted to show what a fantastic officer he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for example, if this report was written up by General Zivanovic, corps commander, it would be inappropriate for him to say that he is providing information to his Chief of Staff, reporting to him. If he commanded the action, if he was carrying out this combat activity, then it certainly didn't suit him from a moral point of view for him then to report to his subordinate. That's my line of thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, his subordinate? It is sent to the Main Staff of the VRS Chief of Staff personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is correct that the -- there is an error in the English translation, in the English version. The original is addressed to the Drina Corps, so that should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you aware of that, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I was about to raise it but Your Honour was in the middle of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's obvious, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a P exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any P exhibit which clearly shows mistakes, that should be reported without delay, Ms. Hasan. You even interrupt at the very moment you see it and say: I would like to draw your attention to the fact that we have to ask for a revised translation because it's wrong. Any further questions or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, that resolved the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, now after this correction that this document was being sent to the Drina Corps, are you then saying that if this was done by General Zivanovic he was reporting to himself? Or am I missing something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he wrote this report - and he is the only one who can write a report, the person who commands an operation is the one who writes the report - if he wrote this report and sent it to the address of his own Chief of Staff, it was very illogical for him to report to his subordinate. So perhaps for that reason my name wandered into the picture. From a military point of view it is absolutely impossible, given the duties that I was carrying out there, that I should be the signatory of a report on an operation that is being carried out by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to now return to the communications network of the Drina Corps and call up 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the previous document you've shown to the witness, if you want that to be in evidence, then I'd suggest that you tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would then be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 2983 -- 1D2983, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D906, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then if we could have 65 ter number 31890.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we will have a diagram on our screens. I'd like to ask you if you recognise what is depicted in this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And can you briefly summarise or walk us through what is depicted herein? What devices are depicted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This schematic of the organisation of radio relay communications of the Drina Corps in the relevant period of the war between 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is the schematic showing the organisation of radio relay communications of the Drina Corps accurate to the best of your knowledge and recollection as depicted herein?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. There are tiny, minor, completely unimportant differences between these two schematics, but for the bulk of radio relay communications it is accurate and reflects the true situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whose task it would have been to prepare schematics like this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the witness referred to differences in the two schematics. Is this the first or is this the second, or what are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're looking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean if we are informed that there are differences between two, I wonder whether we are looking at number 1 or number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are looking at number 1 and the English translation of number 1. I believe - I don't want to put words into the witness's mouth - I believe he's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so you say there are differences between the English version and the original B/C/S version. Is that what you wanted to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I only wanted to say that the person who drew this made a tiny, really unimportant mistake right here, because I want you to know exactly where the radio relay device in the left bottom corner of the first schematic, this route ends at the point marked PTT Sokolac, that's where it ends. And then continues a wire communication for a couple of kilometres. It's a tiny correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you say this slightly differs from what was there in reality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. It's a really minor correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you have pointed at where it is. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whose task it would have been to prepare a schematic like this one?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The drawing of schematics is part of planning communications and that is the job of the chief of communications in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could tender this one at this time, Your Honours, and then go to the next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we know where it comes from, Mr. Ivetic. It's an attachment number 2. It is undated. Could you provide further information as to what it was attached and whether there's any date on the document to which it was attached, if it was a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The information I have from the Prosecution for this document which is on their e-court as a 65 ter number is, I believe, that it's undated. I can ask the witness if he knows of any way to narrow down the time range of this document based upon the name in the upper right-hand corner, but beyond that I cannot provide reliable information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, do you know -- have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my earliest appearances as a witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know what time-frame it covers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact date when this schematic was drawn, but generally it reflects the communications we had throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They didn't change during the war in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to what this diagram was attached to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This diagram is a type of diagram that is made when communications are established, to be used as a work document. And it's also created for various variants, such as the planning of different operations. For me personally, it would be a very good work document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether it's a good document or not, I asked you whether you know to what it was attached. If you know, tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is the Prosecution in any way in a position to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We do have information about what this document was attached to and when it's from, if that's helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So this is from a plan for the Krimen [phoen] operation which was an operation planned for July of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misspoke, January of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: January 1994, so -- yeah, so the document was created before January 1994 as far as the Prosecution is concerned -- or in --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Around, yes. But either late -- well, either early 1994 or previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed -- well, you tendered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Tendered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D907, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If, by the way, the document to which it was attached sheds any further light on purpose of it, I don't know whether you want to deal with it in cross-examination or not, but then of course the Chamber would like to be informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just to add, Your Honour, the plan -- I believe the entire plan was disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- well, that's -- whether we hear it from the Defence or the Prosecution, it's clear now where it comes from. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have 1D5361 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, this --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have the B/C/S flipped -- it's upside down. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is another diagram that we have that according to the right-hand corner is attachment number 2 of the Drina plan. How does this compare with the one that we just looked at in terms of what is depicted therein?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principal elements of radio relay communications are the same in this diagram as in the previous one, I'm talking about the elements of radio relay communications of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you've already told us that these types of orders would be attached to communications plans and you've identified that the system itself remained the same through the entire period. What would be the differences, what parts would change from a given point in time to another as depicted on this scheme?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All relay communications of the Drina Corps shown in this schematic were in place and unchanged throughout the war. There's only one communication route that was equipped with RRU-1 was moved and movable. It moved depending on where the Drina Corps was carrying out operations. It was a small portable device and it was the only mobile device and it moved together with the Drina Corps and its current position. All the other communications were fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, do you have any recollection or information that you can provide about what time-period this schematic would relate to, given that it relates to the Drina plan?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names like "Drina," I don't know, I didn't plan the communications so I don't know, but the way the communications are drawn they reflect the communications as they were throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we then tender this one into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But does it mean that you do not know when this document was -- this sketch was drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's probably an operation or a plan that was given that name, "Drina," but I don't know that because I didn't have anything to do with planning, only implementation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic or Prosecution, this again is attached to some other documents. Do we know what the other document is and from when it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I personally don't. This particular ERN by itself I could not find in EDS which means that it is attached to another document. Without knowing the first page of that range, I could not locate the document in EDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, would you have any clue to --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, this is another plan and it's from 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any month?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We'll look into that. I don't have the month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 1993, 1994. You tendered it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But Judge Moloto has perhaps one or more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, just a little observation. In the previous schematic diagram, sir, you referred us to the left bottom corner to PTT Sokolac and there was a little box to the right of this one that is there and a little line showing that the two were connected. I see that little box is not here. Does that make any significant difference or not? And if so, what is the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This little box, as the interpreter called it to me, is the way a stationary communications centre is marked, depicted PTT Sokolac. That's where it indeed was. But the person who drew this took the liberty of placing one thing on one side and the other on the other, which is basically a choice the person has. It doesn't matter to this schematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't express myself clearly. What I'm saying is the previous exhibit had two little boxes here; this one has got only one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the English one be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, the previous exhibit. This is a B/C/S and an English version of the same document, but D907 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we could have D907.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way that we could have D907 to the left and this one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the right. And the original of D907 and then the English version of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Even the original of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This one has a circle and a box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we zoom in to this one, the one on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please zoom in further on the left side, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this really -- does it say "Sokolac"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in even more to the left bottom side of what is on the left part of the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have looked at it carefully. We -- I've one final question. We see lines which are just straight lines and we see lines which look like a telephone cable. What is the telephone cable line standing for and what is the direct line, often with numbers to it, stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, this coiled wire means that these two locations, PTT Sokolac and the location called Knezina, were connected by telephone cable. And this wavy line depicts a telephone cable, it could be underground or above ground. And this straight line is a radio relay communication between two points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that is also expressed by what looks like a parabolic antenna in the symbol a triangle with something on top of it which then depicts the antenna. Yes, thank you. Mr. Ivetic, I think we have no further questions on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it tendered it [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you tendered it. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D908, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D908 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could now have P1624 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is a map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so. Witness, earlier when you said on the other map it's more or less the same, did you as a matter of fact refer to this map which -- this diagram which the Chamber had not seen before? Were you comparing those two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These two diagrams on the screen now are basically from the standpoint of -- of view of the organisation of radio relay connections -- communications of the Drina Corps are absolutely the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at the same time I see, for example, that there is a double connection from Veliki Zep. If you look at those antennas, you see in easterly direction there are five on the one diagram and there are four on the other one. Perhaps we could zoom out slightly on the left one, but you see in the square box -- yes, I see in the left diagram we have four and in the right diagram we have five. That seems to be not exactly the same. Could you tell us how you can reconcile that with saying that it's the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The right one has five lines, that's to say, five radio relay routes. But these two lines, these two radio relay routes that are closest to each other and that are going to the same location, that schematic dates back to the time when at the location Bratunac, for the needs of the Bratunac Brigade, it was envisaged for this second line to go to the airfield in Bratunac. There's an airfield there from the past used for sports planes. And this schematic was just a plan. But the airfield eventually never came to be used so two lines were never established, only one, and that was the connection with the Bratunac Brigade. The left schematic is more recent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I stop you there. We are looking at two diagrams which both reflect plans, so to say what happened we cannot see that on this diagrams because these are just plans, as was explained to us. Now, I see that at least these plans there is -- in this respect there is a difference, which you just explained to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could take a look at P1624. This will be a map from the Army of BiH, the counter-electronic warfare service of that army and it, according to the left top corner, is from January 1995 to September 1995. I would like to zoom in on the intersecting lines that converge at the bottom right of the map if we can. A little bit more. A little bit more. A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recognise the geographic locations that are depicted in this portion of this map?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although the resolution is rather poor now that you've zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we could zoom out one level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that better, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe go back to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a hard copy of it, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't have a hard copy of this one. I do have an electronic copy but that's not going to help us since the witness would not be able to mark the electronic copy unless it's in e-court. Every time they go into e-court they come back with the same resolution, I believe, unless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- bringing it into e-court would not assist in making the resolution any better.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It can be worse or the same. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have hard copies of this map if it would be of assistance, we can get those during the break or send someone in to bring them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're almost at the break, so I can perhaps ask some questions without the use of the maps and then if the counsel are able to give us one that could be marked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- then we can do that. We would appreciative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, your assistance is very much appreciated, Ms. Hasan. And we'll take a break in five minutes from now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, first of all, could you tell us, did you have a chance to review this map during proofing?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, in relation to the area of -- the geographic area that is depicted here, which area is it that is depicted in this portion of the map, the lower right-hand corner of the map?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a part of the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps with the radio relay hub in Veliki Zep and it depicts also radio relay routes that supposedly diverge from this hub -- that radiate from that hub.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then, Your Honours, I guess we could take the break now because any other question would confuse us without having a map that we can actually point to and mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take the break now. Witness, we would like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher. We resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, before we continue, is Mr. Lukic, lead counsel, is he around? Because we would like to briefly deal with the request. If he could come to court if -- either at the very end of this session or at the beginning of the next one, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll make sure that that message gets back to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with -- during the break we have received, with the assistance of the Office of the Prosecutor, a hard copy of this same map which we've placed on the ELMO. So at this time I would ask the court officer to activate the ELMO screen for our monitors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's activated. If you push the ELMO button and then you will see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, it's been a little while since we've used that so I was a little bit rusty as to how -- how to effectuate that on my end.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. We do have one in hard copy, Your Honours, if you want to look at it there or if that's sufficiently clear for you, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you have a hard copy available, then we certainly would like to have a look at it. If it's the only one and if you would be handicapped by not having it, then of course we would look at our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We have the original as well. Would you prefer to look at the original?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- any copy which is well legible is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO can be adjusted to make it more clear on the screen. Could the usher assist and try to make it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think if we unfold the bottom and lay it flat, it should assist with the focusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the resolution be made more accurate. I think this seems to be the optimal situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's clear enough. Of course the witness can look at the ELMO version --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- directly. We have a version before us, and I'm still on good terms with my colleagues so we can -- we'll share one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You can share.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, based on your information and knowledge, is what is depicted here accurately representing the VRS communications network? And I'm only talking about the area in relation to the Drina Corps that we're zoomed in on.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, could you first mark with an X and then a sequential number starting with a 1 each of the components of this map which you want to identify as being inaccurate and after marking each one give us an explanation of what you know about this component, including a description of what is accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I will start from the south, that is to say, from number 6.
