Veliki Zep, then further on this black line where it says "Veliki Tmor," it never existed before the war, during the war, or after the war. It is marked in dark black, so whoever drew this map knows that this is a very important relay line with a lot of channels; however, it never existed, this radio relay route.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- hold on, and for the purposes of the record, you have now put an X and a number 1. Where have you put the X and a number 1, what is depicted there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The radio relay between Veliki Zep and Veliki Tmor, that is to say, between two features, and this radio relay axis never existed and it's not on the schematic or diagram that we looked at today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what we see here under the name "Panorama" which seems to be in the centre of this relay network, is that what you call Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Veliki Zep is the top of this mountain, trig 3527 metres. Panorama for a while was the code name for the communications centre of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska that was at the foot of that mountain, Veliki Zep. That is how it is depicted on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So where we read "Panorama," it is next to a mountain and that mountain which is at the centre of the communications here, that is what you call Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Veliki Tmor, that is in small letters at the bottom of the map between 84 and 86, where the line ends which you crossed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Veliki Tmor is a topographic feature that is an extension of this line; however, whoever it was that drew this map did not have -- I mean that side, if you will, so this relay route could not have continued to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It didn't exist. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could, sir, now go ahead to the next point on the map that you wanted to identify and explain to us -- first by marking with an X and by putting the number 2 next to it and then explain for us what you wish to say about that particular aspect.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next one is this line that denotes the radio relay between Veliki Zep and then further on towards the town of Pale, where the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was and the Presidency of Republika Srpska. However, our actual communications were not organised with this azimuth and in this way. Rather, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the Presidency had communication from Veliki Zep to Jahorina, and then on Jahorina there was an intermediate station for Pale. So Pale is at the foot of the mountain and there is no optical visibility with Veliki Zep and that is why a completely different direction was taken towards Jahorina. So this Veliki Zep-Pale that is marked on this map is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the record, could you mark that with an X and a number 2, that part that is incorrect from Pale to Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness needs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be provided with a pen which works.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, using the pointer, that is to say, not drawing on the map but using the pointer, could you show us the direction that this communication actually went to Jahorina and then to Pale. Show Your Honours what route actually was taken for those communications.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here on this map we cannot see Jahorina because it is to the south from here, so I would need another map in addition to mark that part. At any rate, it's to the south but not under this azimuth where the town of Pale is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now could you move to the next point that you wish to tell us about, first mark it with an X and the number 3 and then describe for the members of the Panel what comments you have to say about that element.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is marked here is the radio relay route between Veliki Zep and the command of the 2nd Romanija Brigade of the Drina Corps. Purportedly there was a communication between Veliki Zep and the town of Sokolac. It says "Bresa" here, that is the secret name, the code-name, of this brigade, and whoever it was that drew this map wrote in red "the Sokolac Brigade" up here. However, this route did not exist at all. As for communication with this brigade because there is no optical visibility between Veliki Zep and Sokolac, we had to organise it through the Strazbenica hub that is all the way in Montenegro, the state of Montenegro to the south. And then this intermediate station had a completely different azimuth, so it rechannelled, if I can put it that way, the communication towards Sokolac. So this axis never existed and whoever it was who drew this map did not know how communication was organised to the 2nd Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now for the next element could you mark it with an X and the number 4 and give a brief explanation of your comments relative to the accuracy or the inaccuracy of the same?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And it would be very helpful if you can slow down while speaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next marked radio relay route to the alleged units of the 2nd Romanija Brigade absolutely never existed. Within the brigades, we never had battalions that had radio relay communication. So this route never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you're referring to what you have now marked with an X and the number 4; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now could you please first mark with an X and with the number 5 the next element of this map that you would like to give us a brief comment upon.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, this route that I marked with a number 5, that never existed either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you move on to the next element of the map that you have a comment upon, mark it with an X and the number 6 and give us your explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before he does that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- could we find out between which two points is number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we move a little bit further to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still a bit more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Over here on the map he linked some two locations where we did not have any commands or radio relay routes. Quite simply, this was drawn -- I mean, I didn't draw this map, none of our members did, so I simply find this illogical how somebody could have marked something like that, the existence of a radio relay route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know what the names of those two points are at the end of the line, either side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are two elevations, heights, hills. It's very hard to read this because the map is so small, but I assume that whoever it was that drew this map thought that we had points as high up as possible in order to have optical visibility. However, in this area we had no need whatsoever for radio relay communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, before we continue, could we learn what this map -- is this a plan or is this an abandoned plan? Because the witness says that nothing is - until now - is what it looks like. So therefore I'm wondering --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I can answer that, Your Honours. At transcript page 13337 we had Prosecution Witness RM279 testify that this map was created by the ABiH in 1998, relying on the information of analyses of intercepted VRS communications from 1995 and at that time it was introduced into evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just have a look. So this depicts then, if I could say so, the enemy communications?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, the enemy's -- the VRS communications that the enemy was supposedly listening to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. ABiH depicting what in their view the enemy --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- communications were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I meant with "enemy communications."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you -- well, I'll look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- is the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you now move on to the next point in the map that you wanted to comment on, mark it with an X, and identify it with the number 6 and give us your explanation of why it is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This line marked here on the map between Veliki Zep and Han Pijesak as a radio relay communication, I allow for the possibility that this did exist, or rather, this radio relay communication did exist. Now, could you please tell me how it is that I'm supposed to mark it as opposed to the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we're only marking the ones that are inaccurate or that you believe are inaccurately reflecting the actual situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we put a little circle, a little O around that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- line or over that line so that we know that you have testified about that line and possibly -- either existing or possibly existing. So if you could make just a little circle which includes the line, then ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This communication did exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps it would even be best to give that a number as well, so that we know the cross with the numbers and the circles with the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you make that a 5 then -- I think we -- were we at 5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A 6, could you add a small 6 next to the circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it almost looks as if it was 60 but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At least it will be identifiable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let's move on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could now mark the next location you want to talk about with the number 7, and if it's incorrect an X, if it's correct an O, and then give us an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This communication, this radio relay communication never existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, just for completeness of the record, where the witness put a little circle, he later crossed out that circle in a way as which in computer language you make a zero. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you've identified already for us - let me just see - the -- the item you marked with a 7 as not existing, what are the end points at each end of the alleged route?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end point was Veliki Zep and here, this intersection of roads, it says "Ravanjsko."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is there any other element in this map that you wish to comment upon as being inaccurate depicting the routes -- relay routes of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that next route with an 8 and an X and then give us an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This radio relay route between Veliki Zep and an elevation here, it's called Viselac, above the town of Vlasenica. In Vlasenica that's where the corps command was, in the centre of town, and on the building of that corps command, that is to say, on the roof of that command building, we had an antenna and equipment. Whoever it was that drew this map went here, about a kilometre and a half to the west, and he thought that we had relay equipment here, but we actually had it here in town on a roof-top, on the roof-top of that building. So there's a big difference in azimuth of some 5 degrees. Although now I am at a loss as to whether I should cross this out as such; however, it is inaccurate since we had equipment in town itself, not on this hill about a kilometre and a half to the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that route that you've been talking about with an X and the number 8.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and here X not standing for a non-existing communication but one that is plotted not correctly --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- according to the witness on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe so your pen doesn't dry up, close it in between using.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are there any other elements on this map that you believe are inaccurately recording the actual situation of the relay routes of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next one, from the corps command to Veliki Zep we had two radio relay communications, and here the second one hasn't been marked at all; that is to say, only this one, the one that I crossed out, was marked and it's not placed in the best place, but the second one that we had was not marked at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you explain --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- what you mean by "was not marked at all"? We can't see the end of the line because the map has to be moved a little bit further to the bottom left side. But what do you mean by this term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to say that according to the diagram of communications, from Veliki Zep to Vlasenica we had two routes. Whoever it was that drew this map envisaged only this one, but he did not know of the existence of yet another one that we had up to here, to the town of Vlasenica, which I also consider to be lack of knowledge of communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As you said earlier, the line doesn't end in the town but on an elevation and that was wrong, this was marked as X 8. And little bit further to the east there is the correct line missing. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is to say, a bit further east in town itself there should be two lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just take a follow-up on that one. Does this line marked number 8, is it not possible that that is the second line that you say ended up in Vlasenica? Maybe incorrectly placed, but intended to be the one that is missing -- that you say is missing? I'm asking this because the one line on the east goes past Vlasenica, but this one, although not on the roof of the top -- on the roof of the building, does end around Vlasenica. Could it be that that is the second line that you say is missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This line that I intend to cross out now is a link between Veliki Zep and the Birac Brigade in Sekovici, which also did not exist so I'm going to cross that out later. But I'm saying once again, in the actual plan of communications from Veliki Zep to Vlasenica we had two lines. Whoever it was that drew this map just envisaged this one and at a wrong place in that. He did not know of the existence of yet another one at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You have explained it better for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you now move to the next one, to Sekovici, that you said you also wanted to cross out later, could you mark that with an X and the number 9 and give us your explanation.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relay route never existed. With Sekovici we organised communication round -- in a roundabout way. Four hubs were involved with a completely different azimuth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Why did you need to organise communications with Sekovici via four different hubs; what was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the brigade command in Sekovici is in a valley and there is no optical visibility to Sekovici, so we had to go around in order to establish communication because the equipment that we used needed optical visibility in order to establish communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other elements of this map that you believe are inaccurate that you would like to discuss with us in court?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would just like to ask kindly where this line ends finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could move the map, I guess, down and to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This route on here connects two points Veliki Zep and a place called Osmace Tactical Group. Due to the absence of optical visibility we never had a radio relay route with a command in Osmace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then could you mark that one with an X and I believe we're up to the number 10.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are there any other elements on this map that you consider to be inaccurate that you would like to discuss with us in court today?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This next radio relay route connected Veliki Zep with the communications hub at Crni Vrh, Gucevo, in Serbia. However, we never had such organised communication with the hub at Crni Vrh. Instead, it went from Veliki Zep to Mount Cer, and from Mount Cer to Crni Vrh, so that this radio relay route, the next one that was drawn, never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark with an X and the number 11 this one that never existed.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again could you explain for us why you had to go through the relay hub at Cer to reach the -- Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there's no optical visibility between Veliki Zep and Crni Vrh. Instead, we had to take a roundabout way using hubs where there is optical visibility under a completely different azimuth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are there any other elements of this map that you consider to be inaccurate that you would like to describe for us?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next one is between Veliki Zep and Milici, that is to say, the Milici Infantry Brigade, because there was no optical visibility with the command of the Milici Brigade, we never had this route. We had wire communication with that brigade from Vlasenica and we didn't need the radio relay communication, and that one is drawn on the radio relay communications plan. This radio relay route never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the one that never existed, could you mark it with an X and the number 12.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And could the map be moved more to the left side. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are there any other inaccuracies that you would like to identify for us on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next radio relay route with this device drawn in black is absolutely unclear to me. We never had a unit there whatsoever and we never had any radio relay route in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that one with an X and the number 1-3, 13.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you identify for us the end points of that alleged radio route, the locations of the end points of each end.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That radio relay route connects features of Veliki Zep and it says here "Bisina," if I'm reading correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are there any other radio relay routes of the Drina Corps depicted on this map that are incorrect that you need to discuss with us?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This radio relay route drawn in black connects the radio relay hub of Veliki Zep, ending at Avala, Mount Avala near Belgrade. If I see right, that route did exist but it didn't take a straight line like shown here. Instead, it went first to Mount Cer and from Mount Cer to Avala, whereas this map shows a direct line from Veliki Zep to Avala. You can see that if you unfold the map because Mount Cer is approximately in the same direction. But in any case, there was not a direct route from Veliki Zep to Avala, it had to go through the hub at Mount Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could we mark --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, what I just tried to explain now, if you can see well, this is an uninterrupted line ending at Avala near Belgrade. That was also not a direct line. It went through the hub at Mount Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For that line that you've just identified could you put a number 14 and also an X indicating an incorrect route.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the witness be provided with another pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps put away the other one. Could I ask the witness one question. A minute ago you told us that the line to Mount Cer did not exist, and you are now telling us that this first stretch to Mount Cer was part of a non-direct line with Avala, I think you said, or Kavali -- Mount Avala. Now, I'm a bit confused. If you have this first part of the route at Mount Cer, that means that there is a connection between Veliki Zep and Mount Cer. And a minute ago you told us that there was no such connection, no such radio relay. Could you explain how we have to understand this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It must be an error in interpretation. I said there was no radio relay connection between Veliki Zep and Crni Vrh. Maybe the interpreters confused it, maybe they confused Crni Vrh and Cer. That was not my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or I misunderstood it. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can assist, Your Honours, page 60, lines 2 through 13, seem to imply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- that they had to go to Cer to get to Crni Vrh, and that the line from Veliki Zep to Crni Vrh did not exist as a straight line. I think that's the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not -- let me re-read it. One second. So sometimes you say the radio relay route may have been there but not as plotted on this map, where it's sometimes plotted as a direct route and that's true for Crni Vrh and now for Mount Avala, that there was radio relay -- there was a radio relay system, but not as depicted on this map. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not quite. This radio relay route plotted as it is on this map, showing a direct connection between Veliki Zep and Avala near Belgrade, never existed. Instead, to Avala you had to go through the radio relay hub at Cer, that is to say, Veliki Zep-Cer and then Cer-Avala.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the relay existed but in two steps and not as marked on this map in one direct relay. Please -- Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we just get some clarity if the witness can show us where Mount Cer is that he's been referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would make it easier to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we can mark Cer with a 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps. Could you tell us where that Mount Cer is. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map is very difficult to read because of its scale, but Mount Cer is a mountain overlooking the town of Loznica. It's somewhere in this area. And this connection could not be made over such a large distance. So instead, it had to go through this mountain. If I had a different, easier map to read I could more easily find that location. In any case, it's somewhere here in this sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see on the map, using my best glasses, "K Cer" which is at just -- let me find it again, which is just below south of Gornji -- is it Bornja [phoen] -- could you --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this will just make it a bit simpler. If we look where it says "K Avala," there is a triangle which is depicting a station and you see just in the middle of it it says "Cer."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see there -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we just move the map on the ELMO a little bit so everyone can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we see on Mount Avala, we see the letters "C-e-r" from what I see. Do you see that? And what does that stand for? Do you know whether that's Mount Cer or is it not what you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, my mistake. I read "Avala" here. So on this map, which is not our own military map, I thought it was a relay connection to Avala avoiding Cer. So at the beginning there is Avala and this radio relay route 14 did exist. I'm sorry, I made the mistake because this is not a military map that I normally deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I then understand well that where it's written "Avala" or "Avali," that that indicates, as it often does in the margin of the map, where -- to what destination the route continues? So we have to read now the line connecting Veliki Zep to where it is written "Ka Avala," where we find next to the line the letters SMC, to be the first stretch going to Mount Cer, which then continues not visible on this map to -- okay, that's hereby clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And perhaps for number 14, if we can put a circle around the X to denote that that is a correct route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- well, the correct route is with a circle, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness confirmed now that where he depicted X 14, this is a correct line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we make first that circle around the X, it changed from non-existing to existing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you make -- next to 14, could you make a little circle around the X you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were at the right spot a second ago. Could you mark -- could you make a little circle --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just refer to page 63, lines 17 and 18, Judge Orie asked: "So the relay existed but in two steps and not as marked on this map in one direction -- one direct relay," and the witness nodded "yes" but because you didn't say it verbally it didn't come on to the record. I just wanted the record to show that you did answer that question and said "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But this was corrected later. It was I think -- I don't want to repeat that, it would confuse it even more, but at the end the witness said this is depicted correctly in the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the parties do not disagree on that the witness confirmed that it was a two-step relay which he thought was not properly plotted, but the parties both have heard and as has the Chamber that the witness confirmed that it was a two-step --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- explains why there is an explanation -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are we finished with all the inaccuracies or are there more inaccuracies you wanted to point to our attention on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to say concerning the inaccuracies that there was never a direct radio relay route between Veliki Zep and what is marked here as the Skelani Brigade although it was the Skelani Battalion. So this route never existed. Communication with the Skelani Battalion was organised in a completely different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that one with an X and the number -- I think we're up to 15.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does that complete your review of all the inaccurate parts of the Drina Corps communications network as depicted in this map?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's also drawn here that communication with the Rogatica Brigade, whose secret code-name was Domar, was organised directly from Veliki Zep towards Rogatica, which is completely untrue. Because there was no optical visibility between Veliki Zep and Rogatica, this communication was organised via a feature Strazbenica in Montenegro, so this is completely inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that with an X and the number 16.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now have we completed your recitation of incorrect radio relay routes of the Drina Corps on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this map at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As marked, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then we have to -- the map is now on the ELMO, therefore it first has to be scanned and uploaded into e-court. Therefore, the map as marked should be given in the hands of the Registrar and then -- or would you -- I don't know whether you have the technical facilities to upload it or whether it has to be scanned in any technical way. Could you please organise this together with the Registrar so that we have finally a good copy in e-court and I think the original one should be kept as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, that's fine. Perhaps you should MFI it instead of entering it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although it's due to these technicalities that's -- unless Ms. Hasan would have any objection against admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I just had two points of clarification in relation to the witness's testimony I thought might be easier to deal with now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it always --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- I can address it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it -- of course I do not know what you are going to say, I also do not know whether we -- you think we would need to hear that right away or would it --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I just think it might be helpful. But I can briefly just tell you and that is the -- you know, we've been referring to a -- you've heard a lot of evidence about a station called Gucevo and we've been looking at this map and the witness has marked and spoken about a certain link, and I think it would help Your Honours to know whether Gucevo is a station represented on this map and whether the witness has addressed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, would you have any problems in this being addressed at this moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Not at all, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at all. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, could you -- are you familiar with a communications station or node that's called Gucevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- yes, your question is now asked by the Prosecution - that's a bit exceptional - but the question is whether you are familiar with a Gucevo communications station? You are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Gucevo is the same as Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That clarifies it apparently well. Then you can move on -- well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We still --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Judge Moloto may have another question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- need a number reserved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we still need a number. Mr. Registrar, the number reserved for the map which is now still on the ELMO but will be soon in original in your hands and in e-court would be MFI'd under number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D909, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the time being. You said 90 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D909.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D909 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to move to D879 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, maybe I should ask a question about the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- before you go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to find out if somebody is plotting radio relay lines on a map using as his source interception of telephone communication and the two people talking are speaking on a line that is not straight but goes via, would that person be able to identify that that line is not straight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That person, if they are listening in on a conversation, has to have his antenna directed the same way, in the same route as the conversation that's taking place. Sometimes three different communications nodes are used. That person with his antenna has to be at least in -- following the direction of one of them. His antenna has to be turned to face that route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would the short answer be: Yes, he should be able to see that the route is not straight? Or is the answer: Yes, he wouldn't be able to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That person could not know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, perhaps to follow-up on that area. If we're talking about an RRU-800 device, in order to intercept both sides of a conversation relayed by that device, how many listening posts would the enemy side need to have to hear both sides of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio relay devices RRU-800 work in duplex, which means that the transmission and the receiving frequency are separate, which means that a participant is listening in on one frequency and speaking on another. And on the opposite side, it's vice versa. The person who is trying to listen in on that conversation has to find himself first on the same straight line along which this conversation is taking place. And for good-quality listening, he has to have two receivers, and with one receiver on one frequency to listen to one participant and with another receiver on a different frequency to listen to the second participant because the transmission frequencies of the two participants are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we assume that the two original participants on the VRS node are points A and B, in relation to points A and B where would those two listening nodes of the enemy side have to be situated?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best place for this station is to be between points A and B, that is to say, at some point C that is between A and B, and from that point there should be optical visibility with both sides. And then on one frequency they listen to one participant and using another frequency they listen to the other participant, and then this is compressed and then the entire conversation is obtained. That is the best way of intercepting communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But did that scenario -- I take it they would have to be in between -- is there -- let me take that back and start again. What about any possibility of having listening posts that are not located on enemy territory, that is to say on VRS territory, where would the listening post have to be if not located in between A and B to hear both sides of the conversation, again using the A and B designations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In such cases it is best for that listening post to be an extension of this line, the straight line linking A and B, either after A or after B. However, in such situations the listening post can hear only that frequency coming from one participant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then where would the other listening post have to be situated to hear the other part of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One listening post should be situated before point A -- or rather, behind point A and the other one behind point B, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or between A and B still? Not necessarily beyond B, but could also between A and B, whereas the other one is, to say so, before A. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correctly understood, but Mr. Ivetic asked about situations when it is impossible for it to be between A and B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would your answers be any different if it was an RRU-1 radio relay device in question?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have the same characteristics as far as electromagnetic waves are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were there circumstances in the Drina Corps where both an RRU-1 and an RRU-800 were both used to convey a single communication?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If between them there is a node and if this communication is between these two stretches. So in one the communication is through RRU-800 and this same communication is conveyed through RRU-1, such possibilities exist as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about on the same line? One direction being RRU-800 and the other direction being RRU-1, did that exist in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely what I have explained, that that is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now in order to be able to follow both sides of such a conversation conveyed over both an RRU-1 and an RRU-800, how many locations would the other side need to have as listening posts to hear both sides of that conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the best-case scenario would involve two groups. One would have to be along the stretch where RRU-1 is and it should be between points A and B, and the other group that would be listening in would be listening to what is conveyed through RRU-800, again ideally being between points A and B. In all other circumstances, it is four groups that are indispensable, four groups to listen in in order to have a quality recording of a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd now like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we can take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you earlier said that Mr. Ivetic asked you about where it would be impossible to be between A and B, I think he said that if it was on VRS-controlled territory. So there was an implied assumption that there was no way of intercepting anything as long as the signal travelled through -- between A and B travelled exclusively through VRS-controlled territory. That's what is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Between A and B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- implied.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Between A and B, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Between A and B. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00, after the witness has left the courtroom. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Lukic back? Not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We've sent a message and we have to check to see. He should be here or he should be here shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if he's here -- because we want to deal with the examination of the witness, we could do that after the break as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be preferable. I'll make sure he's here at the beginning of the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then start after the break with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with the examination of the witness, there are two matters which I would like to deal with -- or perhaps even three. The first one is the request by the Defence that Mr. Sasa Lukic would be allowed to examine witnesses in court. It was on the 16th of February that the Defence requested that Mr. Sasa Lukic be permitted to examine witnesses. The Defence provided further information on Mr. Lukic's background on the 17th of February, and the Prosecution indicated that it did not oppose the request. The Chamber has some concerns about granting the request mainly because Mr. Sasa Lukic was involved in situations of questionable statement-taking practices in the past. I specifically refer to the discussions in court on that topic with regard to the statements of Defence Witnesses Batinic and Sehovac. The discussion in court revealed possible misconduct by Mr. Sasa Lukic. Lead counsel for the Defence even admitted to certain misconduct when he stated that he, and I quote you, Mr. Lukic, "screamed at his investigators." This can be found at transcript page 22605, not the screaming but the expression by Mr. Lukic. Despite these concerns and also considering the Defence's workload, the Chamber hereby grants the request, however, only on a limited basis. Mr. Sasa Lukic is permitted to examine one of the upcoming witnesses and make related procedural submissions. For any examinations of other witnesses, new authorisation must be sought. As is the case with Mr. Ivetic and Mr. Petrusic, during an examination conducted by Mr. Sasa Lukic, lead counsel or co-counsel for Mr. Mladic must be present in the courtroom in order to supervise. I again stress that counsel is instructed to very carefully supervise Mr. Sasa Lukic in light of prior incidents and the Chamber will do the same in accordance with its duty under Rule 90(F). I should add to this that the Chamber just received or had a look at the original of Mr. Mladic agreeing with Mr. Sasa Lukic examining witnesses in court, which should be filed. Then I briefly with another matter, which is about the video-conference link motion for (redacted) and the testimony of other -- sorry, yes, we have to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue I'd like to read one other decision. The Chamber will now deliver its decision on the expertise of John Clark in regard to the exhumation of the Tomasica mass grave. On the 26th of August of last year, the Prosecution filed a notice of disclosure of John Clark's expert report related to the Tomasica mass grave pursuant to Rule 94 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. On the 18th of December, the Chamber granted the Defence request of the 8th of September for an extension of time to file its Rule 94 bis(B) notice. The Defence responded on the 22nd of December, objecting to the Prosecution's notice of disclosure of expert reports related to the Tomasica mass grave. The Defence submits that the Prosecution be ordered to supplement its submission regarding Clark to meet the minimum threshold required by 94 bis or alternatively that Clark be disqualified as an expert and that his report be rejected. While the Defence does not dispute Clark's knowledge and expertise in the field of forensic pathology, it contends that this report exceeds the scope of his expertise and it takes issue with the strong suspicion of bias in parts of the report. The Defence also challenges the methodology and reliability of the proffered report. With respect to the applicable law concerning expert evidence, the Chamber recalls and refers to its 19th of October, 2012, decision concerning Richard Butler. On the basis of Clark's curriculum vitae, the Chamber is satisfied that he has specialised knowledge in the field of forensic pathology. Such knowledge may be of assistance to the Chamber in understanding issues related to the evidence on the exhumation of the Tomasica grave-site. In this regard, the Chamber also notes its decision of the 24th of May, 2013, recognising Clark as an expert. With regard to the Defence request to cross-examine the witness, the Chamber notes that the Prosecution plans to call Clark as part of its re-opening case. The Defence therefore will have the opportunity to cross-examine him. As for any of the arguments raised by the Defence related to the methodology, reliability, and exceeding of expertise of Clark's report, the Chamber considers that these are matters that can be and should be addressed during the cross-examination of the witness. The Defence will also have an opportunity to fully explore the witness -- the witness's alleged bias in the course of cross-examination or can address it by means of an expert opinion in reply. Based on the foregoing, the Chamber decides pursuant to Rule 94 bis that Witness Clark may be recalled to testify as an expert witness and shall be made available for cross-examination by the Defence. It denies the Defence request to order the Prosecution to supplement its submission and denies the Defence request to disqualify John Clark as an expert. The Chamber defers its decision on the admission of the report and its annexes to the time of the witness's testimony. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Perhaps we could very briefly deal with a remaining matter from the testimony of Vladimir Radojcic. On the 15th of December of last year, the Prosecution brought to the Chamber's attention via an e-mail that Exhibit P6955 was also admitted as Exhibit P4424. On the 23rd of January of this year, the Chamber inquired in court if the Defence had any objections to vacating Exhibit P6955. On the 26th of January, the Defence e-mailed the Chamber, advising it that it had -- that it objects to the translations of P6955 and P4424. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to mark P6955 as not admitted and invites the Defence to liaise with CLSS to request a verification of the translation of P4424. And the Chamber further establishes for the record that the associated exhibit to Witness Radojcic's statement 65 ter 1D2153 corresponds to the exhibit admitted as P4424.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, apologies for continuing with other matters when you entered the courtroom. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his examination-in-chief. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could please have D879 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it depicts?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report in which the chief of communications of the Drina Corps sent information about radio relay communications to the chief of communications of the Main Staff. The essence of this information has to do with frequencies that radio relay equipment in the Drina Corps operated on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge and information, did the Drina Corps change the frequencies used for their radio relay network subsequent to the date of this document that we have before us?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If one were to change the frequencies of the VRS radio relay network, what can you tell us about the type of paper trail or paperwork that would be expected to result from the same?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that kind of activity, an order is required from the chief of communications of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what about at the other levels down the chain and up the chain?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of communications of the Main Staff would, as required, order a change of frequency to one of the head of communications in the corps; and then the chief of communications in the corps would forward that order to the chief of communications at brigade level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would there be any correspondence or paperwork going in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be necessary to send a report on the completion of that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could any individual operator in a subordinate unit to the communications battalion of their own accord change one of the frequencies being used?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you, sir, as komandant of the communications battalion, on your own change one of the frequencies that was being used for radio relay communications?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how about the chief of communications of the Drina Corps, could they of their own accord change one of the frequencies being used for radio relay communications?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could I seek clarification. You were asked whether they could change. Now, are you telling us that they were not -- they did not have the authority to do that or that they practically could not change the frequencies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A change of frequency cannot be done without authorisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you say you can, that is, you're not allowed to do it. But my question was whether you could do it in violation of what you were ordered to do or what you were not allowed to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A change of frequencies is a very complicated procedure. It has to be harmonised with all the other carriers of communication and one could not change frequencies without a detailed plan of communications that was in the hands of the chief of communications of the Main Staff. Because if everybody changed frequencies as they pleased, then total chaos and confusion would ensue because people would be then operating on frequencies used by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, least that would be a risk and the receiving party should be informed about it as well if I understand testimony we received earlier as well. So technically it might be possible but it could give rise to quite some problems and it needed a lot of co-ordination to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be true that the more complex the relay is, that is, several steps rather than in one step, the more complicated such an exercise would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not necessarily. It's a very sensitive affair to change frequencies because many other participants primarily in the civilian structure, such as the television, the police, radio stations, and other broadcasters who have their frequencies on the air know exactly which frequencies can be changed and that plan of communications was only in the possession of the chief of communications, only he could authorise a change of frequency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I made a distinction between authorisation and technically exercising, but I leave it to that. You've answered my questions. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with your knowledge of the technical specifications and the performance of both the RRU-800 and the RRU-1 radio relay devices, was there a technical possibility for them to transmit two channels on two frequencies but for those conversations to bleed over and be heard on other frequencies other than those two transmitting frequencies?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness, in the document that was just shown to you about frequencies, we also read the azimuth which is referred to several times. I always understood the azimuth to be the -- more or less the compass direction in which the signal was sent. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Azimuth is the angle that caps the north direction with the movement of our movement. So if we determine north and draw a line along a circle to the line cutting through the circle along which we move, that would be the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I see always numbers like 28, 40, but nothing above 90 or 120. Is that just a coincidence or did you use a certain specific measuring system for the azimuth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Azimuth is very easily determined on the map and the person who wrote this report probably had radio relay lines plotted on the map and was able to measure the azimuth. So it was the chief of communications of the Drina Corps who indicated these particular parameters for the azimuth. He is the one who made the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but are these codes? Because I see number 7, number 8, 25, 38, but nothing above 40, which would, if you look at a map, would limit the direction of broadcast very much in a very small area. Or is it a reference to a code?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my judgement, this should not be a code because it's our document, it shouldn't be a code. It should be the azimuth expressed in degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then it would only be from north to, well, let's say, north-east that you would take as a direction for sending your signals. Nowhere -- not in any of the other parts of the compass. Which -- is that just a coincidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I didn't write this document. I don't know what the officer who authored it was guided by, but I completely agree with you and what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, it's time to adjourn for the day. You're still on schedule?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honours. I believe I was at two hours and three minutes before we started and I think we added another 20 minutes or so, so we should be about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two hours and 12 minutes are used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I am on track to complete at three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- so most likely you'll finish in the first session tomorrow morning if the Chamber does not intervene again and again. But it's technical stuff and we'd like to understand it and sometimes some questions are needed for that purpose. Witness, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. I would instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any way with whomever about your testimony, same instruction as yesterday. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and with apologies for the delay. We resume tomorrow, the 19th of February, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
